newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh plans to build barrage on the Ganges.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh plans to build barrage on the Ganges.

text.p: Bangladesh Water Resources Minister Abdur Razzak said on Sunday his country was planning to build a barrage to utilise the water of the Ganges following a landmark treaty with India.
"The Ganges and its tributaries shape the life and livelihood of about 40 million people living in southwestern Bangladesh," he told a seminar on water management.
Bangladesh and India signed a 30-year agreement on the sharing of water of the common Ganges river in December last year.
Razzak said: "The long-term Ganges water-sharing treaty between Bangladesh and India has opened a new era of hopes and aspirations of bilateral and regional cooperation."
Under the agreement Bangladesh will receive a minimum flow of 35,000 cubic feet of water per second (cusecs) during the dry season between March and April.

The two neighbours' decades-old water dispute worsened after India built the Farakka barrage in 1954, a dam that curbed the flow of the Ganges, which irrigates much of north India before flowing into Bangladesh.

"Bangladesh can now go ahead with the planning exercise for a Ganges barrage in southern Faridpur ...It will ensure integrated water-resource development in the Ganges basin within Bangladesh by providing irrigation to a gross area of 1.9 million hectares of land," he said.
Razzak said international donors had already shown interest in conducting feasibility and detailed engineering design studies for the barrage.
He said the absence of any permanent water-sharing agreement for the past 21 years had caused a variety of adverse effects in the Ganges-dependent area.

These included degradation of the environment through increased salinity, silting up of streams, scarcity of surface and ground water and decay in the ecosystem of the country's only mangrove forest, the Sundarban, he said.
